explication:
## Purpose and Entry Points
spotatui is a Rust terminal music player with optional Spotify-native streaming and first-class local, Subsonic, radio, YouTube, and Qobuz sources. The primary interactive binary is `src/bin/spotatui.rs`; `src/bin/spotatui-gui.rs` is a second GUI-oriented entry point. The library root is `src/lib.rs`. CLI parsing and non-interactive commands are handled under `src/cli/cli_app.rs` and `src/cli/handle.rs`.

## Bootstrap and Runtime
Startup loads configuration, migrations, authentication/source setup, and constructs application/runtime services before entering the event loop. Runtime orchestration is separated from domain state and UI: `src/runtime/bootstrap.rs`, `src/runtime/startup.rs`, and `src/runtime/pump.rs`. This is an async Rust application using Tokio; feature flags determine which optional sources and AI/MCP capabilities are compiled.

## Core Application State and Actions
`src/core/app/mod.rs` is the central application model, with focused state domains for routing, playback, queueing, source selection, settings, persistence, and screens. User/system intents become core actions, applied through `src/core/action/apply.rs`; this forms the boundary between UI/CLI events and state transitions. Important shared concepts include cross-source queueing in `src/core/queue.rs` and source abstraction in `src/core/source.rs`.

## Terminal UI Event Loop
The Ratatui/Crossterm TUI receives terminal input, routes it by active screen, mutates core state through actions, and renders from state. `src/tui/runner.rs` drives the UI; `src/tui/event/events.rs` and `src/tui/event/key.rs` normalize terminal events. `src/tui/handlers/mod.rs` contains interaction dispatch, while `src/tui/ui/mod.rs` contains rendering. UI code should remain an adapter over `core`, not embed provider or playback logic.

## Provider and Playback Boundary
Infrastructure adapters implement provider-specific metadata, search, library, playlist, and playback operations. Spotify Web/API integration is concentrated in `src/infra/network/spotify_source.rs` and adjacent `src/infra/network/*`; optional source adapters live in `src/infra/subsonic/dispatch.rs`, `src/infra/youtube/dispatch.rs`, `src/infra/radio/dispatch.rs`, and `src/infra/qobuz/dispatch.rs`. Core routing selects an active source and normalizes requests; native/non-Spotify playback uses the internal player path in `src/infra/player/backend.rs` and `src/infra/player/streaming.rs`.

## Audio, Native Streaming, and OS Integration
Spotify native streaming is initialized and supervised in `src/runtime/streaming/launch.rs`, backed by the maintained librespot fork. Audio output, capture, FFT analysis, and PipeWire support are under `src/infra/audio/player.rs`, `src/infra/audio/analyzer.rs`, and `src/infra/audio/pipewire_capture.rs`. External desktop integrations include MPRIS (`src/infra/mpris.rs`), macOS media controls (`src/infra/macos_media.rs`), and Discord Rich Presence (`src/infra/discord_rpc.rs`).

## Automation and Extensibility
Lua plugins run through a scripting engine/API/event boundary in `src/infra/scripting/engine.rs`, `src/infra/scripting/api.rs`, and `src/core/plugin_api.rs`; plugins can observe playback and extend commands/UI behavior. MCP exposes player/history control to AI clients via `src/infra/mcp/server.rs` and `src/infra/mcp/executor.rs`. Optional built-in AI DJ uses local agent CLIs, compatible AI APIs, or local-model endpoints through `src/infra/dj/agent.rs` and `src/infra/dj/brain/mod.rs`.

## Persistence and External Services
Configuration/state paths and persisted playback/history are managed in `src/core/paths.rs`, `src/core/app/persistence.rs`, and `src/infra/history.rs`. Credentials and browser redirects are provider-specific, notably `src/core/auth.rs` and `src/infra/qobuz/auth.rs`. External dependencies include Spotify Web API/Connect, Subsonic servers, radio-browser.info, YouTube via `yt-dlp`, Qobuz APIs/streams, Discord, and AI/MCP clients. `worker-relay/src/index.ts` is a separate TypeScript Cloudflare Worker relay component.
